If it happens Kejriwal is certain to be convicted and may once for all lose the opportunity to become the PM anytime in the future.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What would happen if both the Congress and BJP lost their majority power at the same time in parliament?

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: As the friction between Narendra Modi/Amit Shah and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat continues, it seems Modi may step down after 2025. What’s your opinion on this?

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What would be Lok Sabha 2024 results if BJD, BSP, JD(S) & JJP would have also joined India Alliance?

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: If Congress and I.N.D.I.A alliance comes into power in 2029, then will India become a bankrupt country like Pakistan and Venezuela?

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What if Chandrababu Naidu and Nitish Kumar support the I.N.D.I.A. alliance?

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Is Kejriwal's politics about to be over?

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Will the Congress party always be dependent on alliances with regional parties, as JP Nadda suggests, in order to win elections in India?
Answer: The Congress after its defeat in 1989, the party found to its dismay that they cannot win elections on their own. They need to tie up with other regional parties to form a Government. In 1991 the Congress formed a minority Government under P V Narasimha Rao. In 1996, 1998 and 1999 the party failed to form Government. In 1996 the party contested on its own and failed to even become the largest party. BJP has been the largest party. In 1988 and 1999 NDA formed the Government under Vajpayee. In 2004 the Congress won 145 seats while BJP won 138 seats. There is not much of a difference. But Congress headed coalition formed the Government. In 2009 Congress again formed the Government with its 203 seats. From 1998 to 2024 Congress has been dependent on the regional parties for its victories in constituencies. These regional parties have been once a part of Congress. Because they dissociated from Congress purely for power, they are able to align with Congress. Also when they separated from Congress they took away a portion of support of Congress in their state. Congress started becoming weaker. To fill up the void, Congress formed alliances with the same parties. It initially helped both the parties. Gradually the regional parties became more powerful. They started detesting the Congress. Now TMC, SP, RJD, DMK, JMM, NCP, etc., are dictating terms to Congress. Congress party is forced to accept their terms. If Congress party keeps itself away from the regional parties, the party may not even cross double digit mark. I cannot vouch for Congress to be permanently dependent on these regional parties. What happens in future is not in our hands.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Why did Narendra Modi choose Yogi Adityanath as his successor in Uttar Pradesh? What would happen if Yogi Adityanath was selected as the prime minister of India?

Amit Shah has many successes. His leadership in UP just before 2014 election had a complete transformation in UP where BJP won 71 out of 80 seats. He introduced the abrogation of Article 370 without any untoward incidents. Amit also has to his credit victories in series of state assemblies between 2014 to 2019. Also he is the architect for the general elections 2014 and 2019. He is successful as Home Minister. One negative aspect for Amit Shah not to be selected is he also belongs to Gujarat just like his mentor Modi. This may stand him down. Yogi too has his galore of successes. He has established rule of law in Uttar Pradesh. He completely eliminated the Don culture. He has been developing UP industrially. He has implemented many infrastructure projects, such as Expressways, Highways, Industrial Corridors, Airports both international as well as domestic ones, etc. The Kashi corridors as well as Ram Mandir are the greatest fete of his. Yogi is able to win UP for the second time in 2022. He is the first to be CM for two successive terms. One greatest default is that Yogi botched up 2024 general election of Uttar Pradesh by losing 29 seats. Both are eligible and perfect replacement to Modi. Both have one negative aspect and in all other aspects both are equally balanced.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan

Answer: Every sphere of life is engulfed in politics, whether it is Hathras stampede or the result of by-poll to assembly election or Agniveer or Neet exam paper leaks, etc. These acute politization of incidence are mainly because the opposition could not bend the ruling NDA so far . Rahul did not take the leadership of Opposition in Lok Sabha in 2014 or 2019, because the numbers did not add up to his style of leadership. Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan

People have been voting for the strong and good governance of Yogi. The no nonsense governance of Yogi, is appreciated by one and all. Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan

Hence Congress coming back to power on its own looks not possible. But if there is a perfect alliance without any misgivings between the alliance partners, Congress may cross 150 seats and form a coalition Government. It looks a distant dream. Modi era do not seem to end even in 2029. Probably he will continue to lead BJP in 2029 as well. If BJP forms the government for the fourth time, the opposition will get completely demoralised.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: AIADMK leaders are in a dilemma whether to go for alliance with BJP, in which case they will lose minority community's votes. In case, they avoid BJP, they may miss the votes of Hindus, sympathetic to BJP. What is your advice to AIADMK?
Answer: I personally feel it is better to go in for post-poll alliance, rather than pre-poll alliance between BJP and AIADMK. This will solve one greatest hurdle of seat distribution. DMK is in the decline and both AIADMK and BJP can make the best use of the same by contesting separately.

Question: Is BJP going to loose 2027 UP elections?
Answer: BJP losing or winning hangs by a thread. BJP got 43.31% vote share against INDI alliance 43.52%. The difference of vote share of 0.21% is too minute to say that BJP will lose the assembly election. Also assembly election is a different ball game from the general election. Question: With Narendra Modi again winning as the Prime Minister of India for a third term, does the I.N.D.I alliance have the patience to wait for another five years to try their luck or will it disintegrate before 2029?

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: How many of you think that Rahul Gandhi will step down as the main face of the Congress party if not able to help his party to get 150+ seats in 2029 election?

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What is the reason behind the widespread popularity of the "Modi wave"?

The opposition has been blaming Modi if it rains heavily or drought or a communal violence or even if there is pot holes in roads. the delay in trains or bus is also attributed to Modi. This obsession of the opposition towards Modi took him to new height in popularity. Further Modi right from day one has been concentrating on mega projects whether it is welfare measures or infrastructure projects or introducing new train services like Vande Bharat. His construction of more than 100 airports in different states of the country too added up to his increase in popularity, because no PM attempted such things in their life time. Modi has been hailed by every foreign country. Every country wants to develop friendship with India. People have been awe inspired by the same. The numerous heads of nations reposing their highest honour on Modi only added up to his popularity. Modi’s period is seeing the economic recovery and moving up to the fifth place globally which is a moment of pride for the people of India. The foreign exchange reserve which is surging upwards delighted the people. All these added up to Modi’s increase in popularity. His efforts are reflected in his popularity.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Why is Narendra Modi undefeatable by any opposition parties, unless he himself decides to retire voluntarily?

He approaches the election as a servant of the people. He calls himself a chowkidar. Humility is the hallmark of his approaches in any election. He goes full hog against his opponent whoever he is. So far no leader has been able to defeat Modi. Rahul Gandhi has been trying to defeat Modi since last ten years. He never is able to so far. Honesty is a powerful weapon which never can be defeated.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Will Atishi's Hunger Strike help the Aam Aadmi Party & Kejriwal?

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan

Question: Is Rahul Gandhi trying to give awareness of secularism in Parliament?

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What are the implications of Akhilesh Yadav's statement that the 2024 election marks a moral victory for the India bloc and positive politics?
Answer: The 2024 election is not a victory to the Opposition INDI alliance. The opposition might have increased its numbers no doubt. But not enough for victory. No party in the opposition did come anywhere near the numbers of BJP. The entire INDI alliance is unable to cross the number of BJP alone with all its lies and fake promises. Akilesh Yadav’s statement that the 2024 election marks moral victory is more out of frustration and not out of conviction. His more than 40 seats is the highest the Samajwadi party has secured in its life time. Probably he is elated over the same. Moral victory is useless if you cannot form a Government. Akilesh can only take some vicarious happiness over the improved performance. The lies and misdirection can only take one to certain distance and beyond the same further the path will be very difficult. Only gullible innocents can be convinced with the lies of Khat Khat and all cannot be fooled. This is what happened for the opposition. The opposition never played positive politics, except the politics lies and fooling the public.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Why is PM Narendra Modi Ji elected for the 3rd time too?
Answer: The question is interesting. There are many reasons for Modi getting elected for the third term. Let me assess the same.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Why does Rahul goof up every time he opens his mouth in Parliament?
Answer: Rahul Gandhi goofing up is his wont. The other day he held a pic of Mahadev in the Parliament and stressed that the BJP, Modi and RSS do not own Hinduism. and a Hindu cannot spread violence. Instead of taking the majority community into confidence he has been alluding something towards the same which will not work. He could have done something concrete for Hindus and Hinduism if he really wants to get their support in a big way. Rahul Gandhi holding a pic of Mahadev is exhibiting a weak link with Hindus. It is more like pleading and imploring his concern which is more false and also apparent to the public. By such drama he cannot win over the majority. We have been seeing “the Love Jihad”. When there is his own Congress Government in Karnataka, the life of Hindus are uncertain. Therefore Rahul’s efforts are a wasted one.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Why is Congress behaving as if it has won the election?
Answer: Congress and Rahul Gandhi have forgotten what is victory. They presume 99 seats is victory because they never got such a number since 2014 and presume this as too huge to believe. When the number of seats almost double for a party, the leaders of the party got elated. This number is more than what they deserve or expected. Hence the Congress is behaving as if it has won the election. Congress secured in 2019, 19.66% vote share and in 2024 21.96%, increasing its vote share by just 2.3%. This 2.3% is because of local adjustments with regional parties, complete polarisation of the minorities and Khata Khat promise. None of the reasons are genuine improvements of the support on ideologic basis or on the basis of the acceptance of their leaders like Rahul Gandhi. Therefore these increase in vote percentage will remain a short term gain and will not be a permanent one. If Congress is forced to furrow its own niche in 2029, the possibility of Congress crossing 19% vote share looks daunting. Congress is in a false premise, while the ground reality seams to be giving different image. Congress wants to make the best use of the results by projecting the election a victory for Congress and the INDI alliance.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Do you think general elections will be held in 2026 itself, and so will Modi really win it or will it be INC?
Answer: Will the general election will be held in 2026 depends on whether this government last beyond 2026 to its full term till 2029. Throughout this election in 2024 (36.56%) BJP lost 0.8% of votes compared to 2019 (37.36%). The entire election depends on percentage of votes a party gets. The number of seats a party gets also depends on the same. However strong the opposition tries to shake the ruling NDA, through giving freebies like one lakh per housewife or unemployed graduate, they could not damage the support base of BJP to a great extent because of the strength of glue binding them with BJP. Also the increase in support the opposition got too is too meager. The opposition with all their fake promises could affect the election very marginally. But the same fake promises will not help them in 2026 if a mid-term election happen or 2029. Going through the election right from 2014, it is found that people give importance to credibility, emotional change and continuity of regime. In 2014 the people have been affected by gigantic corruption which got reflected in the results. The opposition to hatred (of Modi) politics affected the results in 2019. In 2024 the promises of freebies of the opposition affected the results. This can be corrected NDA by properly accommodating the aspirations of the people. If there should be a mid-term election in 2026, the NDA government under Modi should fall or become vulnerable. The opposition is depending on JDU and TDP to do them a favor by jumping ship from NDA to INDI Alliance. So far they have said in no uncertain terms that they intend to stay in NDA and there is no intention of severing relations with NDA. Hence the mid term election happening in 2026 will remain a speculation. Even if such a mid-term election happen it will be to the disadvantage of the opposition. Hence the opposition forcing the same is very negligible.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Can the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) win a majority without Narendra Modi?
Answer: BJP did not get majority despite the presence of Modi, but NDA secured majority. Therefore BJP or NDA may or may not get majority even if Modi is leading the alliance. With Modi at the helm BJP did not lose vote percentage or lost very minute percentage of votes less than .34%. Hence it is said the Narendra Modi’s presence is absolutely required to secure majority. Narendra Modi cannot be leading the party for ever. There are many leaders like Amit Shah, Yogi, Devendra Fadnavis, Hemantha Biswa Sarma, Annamalai, etc., who are equally capable leaders to lead the party and the nation. NDA did get majority in 1998 and 1999. Modi was not in the helm of affairs of the party. Also BJP under Vajpayee formed the Government on both occasions. Therefore Modi’s presence is not obsoletely required for victory. Modi himself is dependent on the local leaders to mobilise the support. Hence to call Modi alone made it possible to secure majority is ill founded. Under the leadership of Modi leaders like Amit Shah, Yogi Adityanath, Gadkari, Hemanth Biswa Sarma etc., have developed into national leaders. Hence once Modi puts his papers down, one of these leaders will take over. They are resourceful enough to secure majority for the party too.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Are you surprised that the BJP will go solo in the Haryana Assembly election?
Answer: It is not a surprise that BJP will go solo in Haryana. JJP has been its partner since 2019. BJP has 40 and JJP 10 seats. Together they formed a formidable combination. He may be a powerful Jat leader and has influence among the same group. But there are more claimants for Jaat votes, INLD and JJP too are claiming the Jaat votes. Hence Jaat votes get scattered, while non-Jaat votes gets consolidated under BJP. BJP by going solo is expecting to apportion to itself the entire non-Jaat votes.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Same corrupt Kejriwal who used to call himself and his ministers as staunchly honest, same corrupt Kejriwal and his top ministers are in jail due to corruption, so why has Kejriwal stopped calling them staunchly honest?

Answer: Virat Kohli, a great cricketer, who made his appearance on a high note, has retired reaching his high once again in T20I. This is the moment he has been waiting to cherish. Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Is there a possibility of DMK losing its majority in the next election after Stalin becomes Chief Minister? If DMK does lose, who would become the Chief Minister?
Answer: Muthuvel Karunanidhi Stalin is in for his life’s surprise in 2026. His DMK lost 6% vote share in 2024 and this will only accentuate in 2026. Nobody expected BJP to poach into DMK and all the time it has been believed BJP is tapping into AIADMK. But AIADMK has been firm in keeping its support base intact. In 2026 too DMK will be the one to lose more. In 2026 another actor turned politician Vijay Joseph will make his entry and he will cut into minority Christian votes. DMK is sure to lose some more of its sheen. Annamalai too will be claiming his due from out of DMK because of his incessant attack on the ruling DMK. The 18.5% that BJP+ holds now will bulge into above 26%. Vijay too will end up with 6% to 8%. DMK+ may fall below 30%, AIADMK retaining its 21% is more on the chords. Seeman too will chip in with 6%. In such a scenario, the outcome will be a hung situation, with no alliance getting majority. As it is, it looks confusing and it will be more puzzling in 2026. It is not possible now to say who the CM will be in 2026. But one thing is certain whoever is the CM, will find it extremely difficult to carry on with his work. The demands of the partners will be too high that it becomes beyond the capability of the CM to meet the same.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: BJP now rules 19 states of Bharat, can BJP win those other 9 states in the next assembly elections? Leftists don't waste my time.
Answer: BJP do not have its government in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Kerala, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Delhi. Probably it may happen only after 2031. Now BJP is the main opposition to TMC in West Bengal. BJP is shaping up to be the main opposition to DMK. In 2024 BJP poached into DMK support and grabbed 7% and the party may further apportion to itself another 6% in the next election, when BJP may become the main opposition. Once it happens in the very next election BJP will grab power. This is how BJP is able to come to power in Odisha.

Question: Why do people like Modi and the BJP more than Rahul Gandhi and Congress?
Answer: Modi carries the goodwill of the entire nation. He remains the top leader with highest acceptance. The runner up is way behind him in popularity.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan

Question: What would be the consequences if Modi were to resign or be removed from power?
Answer: Modi resigning is out of question, unless he loses the confidence of the Lower House. As the things stand the alliance partners of NDA deserting the alliance looks remote. Also all the constituents of NDA will not desert the coalition. They are aware of the consequences of joining the opposition INDI alliance. The very idea sends electric shock waves among them. Hence Modi resigning is out of question for the time being. The possibility of some influential parties deserting NDA cannot be overlooked, because the desperate opposition will offer the PM’s position to attract these parties and bring down the Modi Government. Though they ailed initially after the election, it cannot be concluded that the same may make its presence in future. Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Lok Sabha elections, AAP Party did not get even a single seat in Delhi, so should it be interpreted that people of Delhi have already realized that Kejriwal is a highly corrupt, that is why people of Delhi didnot give even a single seat to AAP Party?
Answer: I do not know why the people of Delhi has not iven a single seat to AAP, though the party swept the assembly election. My inference is that the people of Delhi wants Modi and BJP for the centre and AAP for the state. This pattern has been repeated since 2014 and continued in 2024 as well. Kejriwal is an accused of corruption and he is not declared corrupt. Hence your question need modification. After Kejriwal’s dodging the summons of ED, various evidences making its presence and arrest on Delhi Excise Policy corruption may have given an indication of the corruption of Kejriwal. But whether this has reflected in their rejection of AAP cannot be gauged unless the party is rejected in the assembly election 2025 as well. The answer to this question can be had in 2025 only.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Will Rahul Gandhi succeed as the leader of the opposition in the 18th Parliament?
Answer: Rahul Gandhi failed in his first test of electing a Speaker in the Lok Sabha. Rahul announced a candidate by name “Suresh” an MP from Kerala as the candidate of the opposition unilaterally, thinking his candidate will be accepted by all parties. On the other hand most of the alliance partners distanced from the same calling the candidate is not selected on consensus. Rahul failed to take the entire opposition together. The contest for Speaker’s post is not wrong, but the same should have the sanction of all the affiliated parties. Even if he loses he should show that the entire opposition is backing him. Rahul Gandhi should have learnt by seeing the ruling party and Modi, who did not announce the candidature of Om Birla only after the acceptance of all the coalition partners consent. The election of Om Birla became successful one, whereas Rahul has to cut sorry figure with many abstaining or not supporting his candidature of Suresh. In politics arrogance do not have any place. Also nothing can be taken for granted. Always should be cautious and approach every issue carefully.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Will the BJP come to power again after Modiji?
Answer: Bharatiya Janata Party has been going strength to strength after every election. BJP is either ruling or in coalition with other parties in 23 states out of 28. When the party is in control of such a vast tract of land, doubting BJP to come to power in future is a futile exercise. BJP might have lost 63 seats in 2024, but won two new mid-sized states of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.. Also BJP won Arunachal Pradesh. and BJP’s alliance partner won Sikkim. The doubt expressed in the question is because of the sudden drop in numbers in 2024. It is a common phenomena which happens election after election. BJP’s grip over the politics of the nation is strong and firm. BJP also has a galaxy of leaders who are ready to take any responsibility. For another twenty to thirty years BJP will continue to rule the nation. Also the opposition is divided, no common agenda or common ideology. The hosh potch alliance without common goal or ideology will not help the opposition any. Also they do not have unity. Hence this opposition replacing BJP or NDA seems impossible for some time to come.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Will Rahul Gandhi be able to keep the opposition alliance together as the leader of the opposition in India’s Parliament?
Answer: Before the elections barbs have been expressed between Mamata Banerjee and Rahul Gandhi, Pinarayi Vijayan and Rahul Gandhi, Kejriwal and Rahul Gandhi, many more. Mamata Banerjee has not concede even a single seat to Congress. Congress and the Left fought each other in Kerala. Congress also fought AAP in Punjab. The opposition never have been united at any time. After the election Mamata Banerjee raised the issue of Speaker selection. She said that she has not been consulted in the selection of Suresh as the choice of the opposition. Also some parties including TMC did not vote the official opposition candidate. Rahul Gandhi do not have the knack of taking the entire opposition together. He doesn’t know what to talk and when. Rahul Gandhi do not carry any charisma. He is what he is, because of the support of the regional parties. Therefore he never can control the opposition parties and the regional parties controlling him is more true.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What is the reason for Indian Prime Minister Modi's consecutive election victory?
Answer: It is true Modi has three consecutive victories in 2014, 2019 and 2024. In all these elections one common factor is the main opposition remained Congress and Rahul Gandhi. In all these elections Congress and Rahul Gandhi underperformed. The results of all these elections for Congress are their three worst results. Whereas for BJP the results are three best performances. In 2014 Rahul has been harping on the Chai-wala jibe against Modi to give him a good result. In 2019 Rahul came up with Mahagatbandhan in every state and expected to do spectacularly well. He failed on both the occasions. In 2024 he took a different route of attacking Modi through the Constitution in his hand & his Taka Tak, which gave him partial success. He has been able to better his previous best of 52 seats. Modi is able mould the alliance into one single unit fighting its opposition unitedly. Due regard and respect given to each and every partner however small the party is. All seat adjustments have been made in camera, with full satisfaction of both parties. No aspersions thrown openly for the public to watch. All these added up to give an image for NDA and the alliance won the election emphatically.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What challenges might the NDA face in maintaining its alliance leading up to the 2026 Assembly election?
Answer: The alliance of BJP with PMK, Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam, Tamil Manila Congress apart from O Pannerselvam, Dinakaran’s party who contested on Lotus symbol, are to be continued till 2026. It is quite challenging a task. NDA did not win a single seat in Tamil Nadu nor its alliance partners, though the vote percentage have increased phenomenally. If the parties find it not satisfying, they may quit the alliance and walk into DMK alliance if it looks promising. These parties will not go towards AIADMK because there is no hope for them even in AIADMK. Even AIADMK could not open its account. DMK is already saturated as far as its alliance is concerned. Any new parties joining DMK bandwagon will be counter productive to DMK+. Hence parties hopping to DMK may not happen unless that party is too important and has definite percentage of support among the people. DMK too may be constrained to accommodate such parties with limited number of seats. Only if such party is satisfied with the same, will those parties join DMK coalition. The possibility of some joining AIADMK coalition cannot be ruled out, because the party has a well established cadres throughout Tamil Nadu. These small parties need ground support which AIADMK can provide. One advantage NDA hold for them are, they will be satisfied with the number of seats allotted to them and Annamalai is raising as the main opponent for Stalin. These twin effect will more than compensate with the ground situation. With 18.5% votes with BJP+ these parties hope to increase their vote percentage further in the assembly election. Even if DMK loses another 5% to 6% , there will be hung situation which suits NDA. Therefore these parties may not jump ship.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Has Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticized that the Prime Minister is busy saving the government?
Answer: Rahul Gandhi is a known immature leader. He doesn’t know what to talk and when. His criticism that Prime Minister is busy saving the Government do not have any relevance. Modi is able to win the Speaker election comfortably. Also Rahul faced one of his blunder of contesting the Speaker election when he doesn’t have the numbers. Probably to cover up his own bungling, in the Speaker election, he has been criticising the Prime Minister Modi. There is no unity in the opposition. Rahul Gandhi should be concerned with the same. He is not supposed to worry over the ruling dispensation. But his stance seems surprising, giving raise to the sanity of his stand on Modi.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What are the chances that Arvind Kejriwal secures statutory bail in the CBI case?
Answer: The ED, CBI and NIA are bent on keeping Kejriwal in confinement. The Courts have been giving Kejriwal Bail, but the agencies have been putting him back in Jail. Therefore it is a futile attempt on the part of Kejriwal to attempt to seek bail. Kejriwal never will be able to come out of the confinement on bail till this Government is in office. The trial may start at any time soon. Once the same is complete his conviction looks certain. Also other corruption cases including that of NIA case will be hoisted against him. His stay in Jail will only increase as the days pass by because of his entanglement with many more cases.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Why does Arvind Kejriwal keep pointing fingers at Narendra Modi, when Congress is the major culprit here?
Answer: Kejriwal after his debut support in 2013 in Delhi assembly election when he is able to form a government with the support of Congress has reached the height of his ecstasy. Kejriwal believed he being a IITian, Magsaysay award holder and his honesty should be awarded a place in the politics above all others. But the people decided his place in the Indian politics at a place lower than many marginal parties. People failed to recognise him. This angered him. He started pointing fingers at Modi throughout since 2013. He never recognised the popular mandate Modi secured in 2014 and 2019. Kejriwal wanted to become the PM through short cut method. He believed that money can buy him that position, though he has won Delhi without any influence through finance. This wrong notion cost him dearly. Though he made many safe guards like not signing any file or holding any portfolio, Kejriwal is caught in the web of corruption. He is now battling the same day in and day out. Even if he is pronounced not guilty, the shame attached to him in the corruption he will be carrying to his grave. Politically Kejriwal is finished and his desire to be PM will remain his fancy for ever.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: How are people supporting Kejriwal even now after several rejections by Court?
Answer: It is true Kejriwal still has huge support among the people of Delhi. The support may be because of the freebies or because of his hatred towards Hindus. The hypocrisy towards Hindus wearing tilak is only a drama. His love towards the minorities too is attracting huge support among those section of people. Hence his support is based on community and castes. Kejriwal may not win elections but his support may exceed 30%, which is substantial in such circumstance as he is at present. Since AAP stood only in 4 seats of Delhi the support is substantial. when he is going through his lowest period of arrest on corruption case. Definitely Kejriwal’s popularity has taken a hit, but still he has been left with substantial popularity which may not win election for him.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What do you think of Narendra Modi's claim that the country is looking forward to the future but the Congress keeps scratching the past to hide its failures?
Answer: Narendra Modi is forward thinking and always dreams about good and prosperous future for the people of India. He will be striving for the same. Also seek votes on the same promise. Rahul Gandhi on the other hand has been telling the story of his grand mother and great grand father to seek votes. He doesn.t want prosperity and growth. He wants the people to recognise his forefather’s sacrifice and vote him. Both the leaders contrasting in their approach. Narendra Modi wants development in all spheres. Rahul wants cast discrimination to continue and seek votes on the basis of caste and community. Modi is progressive and wants technology in all aspects of life wherever is possible. Rahul is reverse of Modi. He still wants Ballot Paper instead of EVM.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Despite having no solid evidence against Arvind Kejriwal, why is ED so desperate to arrest him?
Answer: These are the evidences available with ED. ED is not desperate to arrest Kejriwal. If Kejriwal is not arrested he is a threat and is sure to erase all evidences or influence the evidence. Therefore ED do not want Kejriwal to be let free till the case is heard.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What is the future of Aam Aadmi Party in Indian politics? Can it become a national party like BJP or Congress?
Answer: The future of Aam Admi Party in Indian Politics is bleak. The AAP itself is made an accused. Kejriwal being the convenor have received illegal money for the election in Goa. ED has evidences for the same. Hence the AAP is made one of the accused. If proved the party will be derecognised. If it happens this is the first time that a political party is derecognised.
